key_insight: A physics-informed token transformer combines symbolic PDE tokens, a neural operator encoder, and an analytic shock-motion prior to accurately track weak solutions of nonlinear balance laws with shocks and steady states.
engineering_relevance: This approach is well suited for fluid and wave problems where preserving wave fronts, stationary states, and geometry-dependent dynamics is more important than pointwise smooth-field accuracy.
method: Tokenize the governing balance law into symbolic inputs.
Use a Fourier neural operator encoder to reconstruct smooth/finite-resolution structure.
Advance shocks with the explicit Rankine–Hugoniot jump condition and learn a correction for residual dynamics.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports tests on moving shocks, stationary shocks, rarefaction waves, and a comparison against a standard high-order finite-volume method, with the Rankine–Hugoniot prior giving the largest gain.
watch_item: Performance depends on access to an explicit shock law and steady-state structure, so applicability may be reduced for systems without analytically known jump conditions or invariants.
paper_title: Physics-informed token transformer methodology for nonlinear balance laws. I. Schwarzschild--Burgers fluid flows
